address: Wibautstraat 78, Amsterdam-Oost (Wibautstraat / Weesperzijde): 1966 eight-storey office-and-flat block, pale brick-and-concrete bands with continuous dark ribbon windows, a crown of square-lattice windows and a glazed supermarket ground storey on cone-shaped piers
notes: Wibautstraat 78 (BAG pand 0363100012129127, built 1966, 145 3DBAG wall surfaces, roof max 31.4 m): the long rounded eight-storey block on the east side of the Wibautstraat with a supermarket at its foot, 63 m by 30 m. Photographed: the east front on the Wibautstraat (w03-70 2025, w05-70 2024, w08-70), the north end (w02-340), the west and south sides (w01-250, w04-160, w06-160, w07-250): pale brick bands between continuous dark ribbon windows on every floor, a crown of two lattice storeys with square windows at the top, a glazed ground storey with a blue Albert Heijn sign under a canopy carried on inverted-cone piers.

walls[0] = panels 47, 89, 7 and 6 (E, 29 m, 21 m and 11 m, eaves 30.3; surfaces 53, 104, 8, 7): 9 storeys of ribbon windows over a glazed ground with an entrance and canopy and ALBERT HEIJN letters on the canopy. walls[1] = panel 41 main part (N end, 26 m at 30.3 m; surface 106): 9 storeys x 8 bays of ribbon windows over a glazed ground. walls[2] = panel 41 east return (surfaces 86 and 45, 9 m, eaves 27.1): 8 storeys, split off because the eaves gate samples the lowest roof along a panel (surfaces 59 and 117 at 21.7 and 15.4 m stay blank). 8 bays per storey on the east front (the photographed rhythm has about 20 window groups; 9-storey ribbon bays at 2.7 m pitch were 13.7k triangles). Simplified: the crown's lattice windows are ordinary ribbon windows, the cone-shaped piers are not modelled, the photographed corners are rounded and the 3DBAG walls are straight facets. Not drawn: the west front (a 4.7 m podium wall in the data under a tower set back behind it; no tidy ribbon read), the south end and the courtyard walls, which stay blank pale render.
Measured 2026-10-14 (measure.ts, evidence in measured.json): groups 0, 1, 2 take the photo's wall and glass colour, window shape, bay count and front class.

Measurement limits: walls[0] reflective window glass under an overcast sky is as light as the concrete spandrels, so the photo glazing is unreliable; ribbon system and bays kept by hand. walls[1] 12 ribbon bays for the triangle budget where the photo has ~25 mullions.
